data.title: ‘Don’t Get Tempted,’ Says RBC About Palantir Stock Ahead of Monday’s Q2 Earnings
data.description:
Next week will kick off with a bang for Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR) with the big data AI company set to release Q2 results once the day’s action comes to a halt.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

The report comes after a period of sustained losses for this one high-flying stock. Since peaking last November, shares have shed 42%.

Given Palantir’s strong record of beating earnings expectations, does that mean the stock offers an opportunity as the readout looms? Not according to RBC analyst Rishi Jaluria.  

“While shares have come down recently, PLTR remains the most expensive stock across our RBC All-SaaS universe at ~40x EV/CY26 and ~30x EV/CY27 consensus revenue estimates, respectively,” the analyst said. “We struggle to underwrite a scenario that justifies current valuation levels.”

As such, ahead of the print, Jaluria maintained an Underperform (i.e., Sell) rating on the stock backed by a $90 price target. There’s further downside of 26% from current levels. (To watch Jaluria’s track record, click here)

Jaluria’s bearish stance is based on several factors. The analyst argues that the company’s recent Commercial segment growth might not be sustainable, pointing to the impact of temporary tailwinds and rising competition from major players including Microsoft, Databricks, and Snowflake, as well as AI-focused rivals such as OpenAI and Anthropic.

Additionally, Jaluria thinks Palantir’s reliance on “selling bespoke solutions with a heavy consultative approach” could curb its long-term market opportunity. The analyst believes this approach primarily appeals to large, complex organizations that lack internal technical capabilities, while limiting the company’s ability to expand into smaller businesses or customers with stronger engineering teams.

Moreover, although Jaluria views Palantir’s Government business as the company’s strongest area, the analyst remains cautious about whether the segment can maintain its current pace of growth. With AI companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI now targeting government and defense markets, Jaluria questions whether Palantir can “sustain its current growth trajectory in these verticals.”

As for the results, consensus estimates call for revenue of $1.81 billion, representing 81% year-over-year growth. However, Jaluria thinks that “for the stock to work,” revenue would need to reach $1.91 billion, which would represent 90% growth and a 5.2% beat versus expectations, consistent with the company’s average outperformance over the past eight quarters.

On profitability, consensus expectations point to a Q2 operating margin of 59.6%. The analyst views a margin of 63.7% as a strong result.

As for the guide, for FY 2026, Wall Street expects annual revenue of $7.73 billion, implying 73% year-over-year growth. The analyst believes a “good outcome” would be around $8.15 billion in revenue, or 82% growth, which would represent a 5.4% beat against the Street.

Among Jaluria’s colleagues, only one other analyst joins him in the bear camp, with an additional 15 Buys and 4 Holds all adding up to a Moderate Buy consensus rating. Going by the $181.24 average price target, shares will be changing hands for a 48.5% premium a year from now. (See PLTR stock forecast)

data.title: ‘Be Smart,’ Says Investor About Intel Stock
data.description:
Wall Street’s debate over an AI bubble has created plenty of anxiety around semiconductor stocks, with concerns over lofty valuations, heavy capital spending, and broader macroeconomic uncertainty dominating the conversation.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) has been caught up in that narrative too. However, an investor with the pseudonym of Esxeleryn Analytics thinks that any “smart bulls” should “avoid AI-bubble hysteria and short-term noise to build long-term returns.”

Esxeleryn Analytics argues that the market is paying too much attention to short-term fears while overlooking what could become Intel’s most valuable competitive advantage. Rather than fixating on the company’s manufacturing roadmap or questioning whether its AI investments are excessive, the investor believes Intel’s greatest opportunity lies in advanced chip packaging, an area that could become increasingly important as AI hardware evolves.

According to the investor, the semiconductor industry is moving away from traditional monolithic chip designs toward heterogeneous Systems-in-Package, where multiple specialized chiplets are integrated into a single package. As AI workloads become more demanding, the packaging layer is expected to play a far greater role in improving performance and efficiency.

The investor sees Intel’s EMIB-T (Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge-TSV) technology and its development of glass substrates as key differentiators. Compared with conventional organic substrates, glass offers superior dimensional stability, lower signal loss, and improved thermal and power characteristics, making it better suited for next-generation AI accelerators. Intel’s partnership with Chinese tech company Lens Technology further strengthens this position. “Through partnering with Lens Technology for precision glass processing and laser manufacturing, Intel is locking in the main bottleneck of the 2027–2030 AI hardware cycle,” Esxeleryn said.

The investor also points to other industry developments as validation of his thesis. TSMC is pursuing similar packaging technologies, while Nvidia has reportedly explored EMIB-based solutions. Rather than viewing these moves as threats, Esxeleryn sees them as evidence that the industry is converging on the same technological direction Intel has been preparing for.  

Another reason for the bullish outlook is the economics of the business. Although Intel Foundry remains unprofitable, the investor argues that advanced packaging requires far less capital than building cutting-edge fabrication plants while offering the potential for significantly higher returns.

“If Intel progressively advances EMIB-T and glass substrates as the industry standard for AI ASICs by 2028, it may capture the highest value-add layer of the AI hardware supply chain,” the investor said. “This will scale up Intel’s gross margins from the current 41.8% to a larger terminal run rate and may justify expanding its ~28x 2028 forward P/E multiple (in my opinion) as analysts’ EPS estimates are progressing upwards.”

Bottom line, Esxeleryn Analytics rates INTC stock a Buy. (To watch Esxeleryn Analytics’ track record, click here)

That, however, is not the most common take among Wall Street’s analysts. While 7 analysts are bulls, with an additional 24 Holds and 2 Sells, consensus rates this stock a Hold. That said, the $119.11 average price target implies shares will gain 28% over the next year. (See INTC stock forecast)

data.title: Why Rivian Stock Is Down Today and Why This Analyst Thinks Its Time Is Coming
data.description:
Rivian (NASDAQ:RIVN) shares are trending lower in Friday’s session even after the company delivered a stronger-than-expected Q2 report, boosted by narrowing losses and improving sales.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

The EV maker reported revenue of $1.66 billion, up 27.7% year-over-year and $90 million above expectations. Its Q2 GAAP loss came in at $0.63 per share, beating estimates by $0.15.

Rivian also raised its 2026 vehicle delivery outlook, now expecting to sell between 65,000 and 70,000 vehicles, compared with its previous forecast of 62,000 to 67,000.

The company reduced its adjusted EBITDA loss forecast to between $1.8 billion and $2 billion, down from its earlier estimate of $1.8 billion to $2.1 billion. It also lowered its capital expenditure guide to $1.7 billion to $1.8 billion, compared with the previous range of $1.95 billion to $2.05 billion.

However, Rivian’s rising cash burn appears to be weighing on the shares. The company burned through $487 million in operating cash during the quarter, compared with generating $64 million in the same period a year earlier. This pushed free cash flow deeper into negative territory, reaching $849 million vs. a negative $398 million in 2Q25.

Nevertheless, for Canaccord analyst George Gianarikas, the quarterly numbers offered a “brief, welcome sunbeam.”

The analyst noted that Rivian’s 2026 EBITDA and capex guidance moved in a positive direction. However, he cautioned that profitability was helped by $108 million in regulatory credits during the second quarter, along with an IEEPA tariff refund receivable.

While Rivian is making progress, sustainable gross margin profitability remains slightly out of reach. Gianarikas expects the second half of 2026 to face additional costs as the company ramps production of its R2 vehicle. However, if production proceeds smoothly and demand remains healthy, 2027 could mark the point when gross margins “break through and should stay sustainably positive.”

In fact, while plenty still needs to go right for Rivian, Gianarikas believes this “may well be Rivian’s hour.”

The analyst said the R2 has received widespread praise and arrived at an especially favorable time. Higher gasoline prices are “casting a fresh glow” on domestic EVs, while traditional automakers are slowing their EV efforts and smaller competitors are struggling.

Demand for the R2 has also been encouraging. CEO RJ Scaringe said on the earnings call that conversion rates from reservation holders are “meaningfully higher” than expected, which Gianarikas viewed as a positive sign given the limited R2 configurations currently available compared with the wider range of options expected in the future. “As new variations roll out in the coming months and quarters, the ticket to ride only gets cheaper,” Gianarikas said.

Gianarikas believes that Rivian previously tried to pursue too many projects at once, including trucks, SUVs, and delivery vans – an “alphabet soup of ambition.” He thinks the company’s current strategy of focusing on one model and gradually expanding its lineup is a simpler and smarter approach.

The analyst also addressed ongoing online concerns about Rivian’s build quality. While he said social media discussions should be viewed cautiously because they can amplify isolated complaints, he believes the issue deserves attention because the R2 is “not merely another vehicle.”

“It is a bet-the-company proposition,” says Gianarikas. “On a ledge that narrow, the margin for error approaches zero.”

Gianarikas, however, seems confident that the company will overcome its challenges, believing that with the R2, Rivian has “caught lightning in a bottle.” As such, the analyst reiterated a Buy rating on the shares, while his $22 price target suggests the stock will gain 36% over the one-year timeframe. (To watch Gianarikas’ track record, click here)

Seven other analysts join Gianarikas in the bull camp, although an additional 7 Holds and 4 Sells add up to a Hold consensus rating. At $18.26, the average price target points toward 12-month returns of 13%. (See RIVN stock forecast)

data.title: Microsoft or Alphabet: One AI Stock Is a Buy, the Other Is Performing Tricks, Says Investor
data.description:
Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) appear intent on never heading in the same direction. The former was an early leader in AI, driven by its partnership with ChatGPT maker OpenAI, while Alphabet trailed behind. But that then changed. As concerns mounted over Microsoft’s soaring AI spending and the returns it could generate, investor sentiment cooled. At the same time, Alphabet won over investors by demonstrating that its AI investments were boosting Search, Cloud, and advertising rather than disrupting them.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Now, following their latest quarterly reports, the pendulum appears to be swinging once again, with Microsoft regaining momentum while Alphabet finds itself facing fresh questions over the scale of its AI ambitions and the mounting costs required to pursue them.

But is that now the natural order of things or is Alphabet poised to usurp Microsoft again?

Looking at both companies’ recent performances, investor Julia Ostian thinks the case for one is much stronger than the other.  

From the investor’s perspective, Microsoft’s latest quarter strengthened the bullish case considerably. The software giant’s shares jumped 15.5% after reporting fiscal fourth-quarter earnings, and in Ostian’s view, the market’s response was fully warranted.

Microsoft produced record quarterly results, growing revenue by 18% year-over-year while maintaining impressive profitability as enterprise cloud adoption and AI demand continued to accelerate. The company’s Intelligent Cloud division expanded by 32% from a year ago, Azure revenue climbed 43%, and commercial remaining performance obligations (RPO) surged 84% to $678 billion.

For Ostian, however, the headline numbers tell only part of the story. The investor argues that understanding exactly where both revenue and backlog originate is essential when assessing customer concentration and long-term risk. “I can’t make my investment decisions when I feel like I don’t have the full picture and the full financial breakdown. But with Microsoft, my worries are way smaller,” Ostian said.

The investor highlights that, excluding commitments from frontier AI model developers such as OpenAI, Microsoft’s commercial bookings still increased 18%. Overall RPO rose 25% YoY, and nearly 90% of cloud revenue for the full fiscal year came from customers outside the frontier AI cohort. The backlog also carries a weighted average duration of 2.3 years, with roughly $203 billion – around 30% of total RPO – expected to convert into revenue over the next 12 months, amounting to a 37% increase in near-term revenue. “Even if not all of the growth comes from regular enterprise customers, the substantial chunk of it does,” says the investor.

Ostian also points to Microsoft’s financial discipline. Despite enormous AI-related capital expenditures, the company continues to generate substantial cash flow, returned $43 billion to shareholders, and trades at roughly 24 times earnings – about 26% below its five-year average valuation.

Accordingly, Ostian rates MSFT stock a Buy. (To watch Ostian’s track record, click here)

Alphabet also delivered strong results, but the market was not impressed, sending shares down in the aftermath, and Ostian thinks that reaction was entirely apt.

As mentioned above, Ostian thinks investors need to know where the revenue and the backlog are coming from, and looking at Alphabet’s recent print, the investor didn’t like the “lack of transparency” on these metrics.

Alphabet has made investment commitments to Anthropic that Ostian views as questionable from a timing perspective. The company invests heavily in the AI startup, which then purchases Google Cloud services, potentially enhancing both the value of Alphabet’s equity investment and its reported Cloud performance. That relationship could make current operating metrics appear stronger, with part of the growth stemming from frontier AI companies. “Google created enormous profitability practically out of thin air while being cash flow negative and continuing to raise CapEx spending,” Ostian noted.

As such, Ostian rates GOOGL a Hold (i.e., Neutral).

Wall Street, however, doesn’t think you need to choose between the pair. Both are rates as Strong Buys. MSFT’s average price target stands at $560.14, offering 12-month upside of 22%. Meanwhile, GOOGL’s shares are expected to climb by 24% over the next year, considering the average target clocks in at $427.81. (See MSFT stock forecast or GOOGL stock forecast)

data.title: ‘Things Have Changed,’ Says Investor About Sandisk Stock
data.description:
Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock, along with other recently beaten-down chip names, surged in Thursday’s trading following upbeat AI infrastructure commentary from Microsoft and Meta, alongside Samsung’s warning that memory supply constraints could persist through 2028. Even so, after a punishing July selloff, the shares remain roughly 45% below their June high.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

Two ETFs to trade SNDK long or short: SNXX & SNDQ

A major recent overhang for Sandisk and the broader memory sector has been the perceived threat from Chinese competitors. Investors became more concerned after CXMT’s successful IPO and reports that Apple was evaluating its memory products, reviving fears of the familiar boom-and-bust pattern that has historically plagued the industry. In previous cycles, strong profitability encouraged aggressive capacity expansion, eventually undermining pricing and profitability, and the market has been quick to price in the possibility of history repeating itself.

However, an investor with the moniker of Quantryon Capital (QC) argues that investors may be overlooking a key structural shift. Management believes this memory cycle will differ from past ones because AI, rather than smartphones or PCs, is becoming the primary demand driver. Speaking at a recent Mizuho conference, the company said data centers are expected to become the largest NAND customer while forecasting bit demand growth in the mid-to-high teens. They also emphasized that long-term customer agreements are intended to reduce earnings volatility rather than simply preserve elevated pricing.

QC also believes AI infrastructure creates a far more durable source of demand than previous memory cycles. Unlike consumer electronics, where inventory corrections can quickly erode demand, spending on AI inference, hyperscale data centers, enterprise storage, and ever more complex AI models requires sustained investment in high-performance storage.

The investor also highlights Sandisk’s evolving product mix as an overlooked advantage. While the company continues to sell commodity NAND into consumer markets, it is placing greater emphasis on enterprise SSDs, a segment management expects to become an important growth driver. Another area of interest is High Bandwidth Flash (HBF), which is being developed specifically for AI inference workloads. Management views inference as a “memory bottleneck” where NAND can offer attractive scalability and cost advantages relative to DRAM.

For QC, the upcoming earnings report will therefore be especially significant. Beyond the headline numbers, the focus will be on management’s outlook for enterprise SSD demand, AI inference adoption, NAND pricing, and competitive developments in China. Street expectations are “very lofty” and have become even more optimistic over the past three months, with only upward revisions taking place, while QC notes that Sandisk has exceeded both earnings and revenue expectations in each of the past five quarters.

In the meantime, QC believes the stock presents a “much more balanced opportunity.”

“I am still bullish on the stock due to the fact that AI-driven demand and product differentiation are still in place,” the investor summed up.

To this end, Quantryon Capital rates SNDK stock a Strong Buy. (To watch QC’s track record, click here)

That is also the conclusion reached by the analyst consensus, a rating based on 14 Buys and 3 Holds. Going by the $2,052.50 average price target, a year from now shares will be changing hands for a 60% premium. (See SNDK stock forecast)

data.title: ‘It’s a Trap,’ Says Investor About Meta Stock
data.description:
Investors did not like Meta Platforms’ (NASDAQ:META) latest quarterly update, with shares subsequently falling by 8%, as concerns mounted over soaring AI spending, an earnings miss, and a steep drop in free cash flow.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

The losses have only exacerbated an already tough year, with shares now down by 30% over the past 12 months.

The question now is whether Meta’s sharp pullback presents a buying opportunity. Investor Julia Ostian argues it does not. Ostian believes this dip “is a trap” as she sees some “serious red flags” once you dig into the details.

Meta made $60.80 billion in total revenue for the quarter, representing strong growth of about 28% year-over-year, while beating analyst expectations by over $514 million. Revenue growth was primarily driven by the core Family of Apps segment, with advertising revenue surging 27% to $59.36 billion.

However, the bottom line paints a far less encouraging picture. Diluted EPS came in at $6.18, missing consensus estimates by $1.22. The biggest concern was a 55% YoY surge in operating expenses to $42.02 billion, which the investor views as the “first major red flag.”

Ostian argues those costs are particularly troubling given Meta’s recent layoffs. She initially questioned why R&D expenses had climbed so sharply after the company cut thousands of jobs. The explanation, she says, came in the form of unusually generous severance packages. According to the company’s 10-Q filing, Meta recorded roughly $1.18 billion in severance expenses tied to an 8,000-person workforce reduction. “This is an incredibly odd decision,” says Ostian, “and it beats me why Meta would do it to the company.”

Beyond severance, expenses were driven higher by accelerating infrastructure investments, rising cloud and AI token costs, and sizeable legal expenses. The investor is especially wary of Meta’s heavy AI spending, noting concerns that the company may already have built more capacity than it can realistically utilize.

Meta’s capital expenditures reached $31 billion during the quarter, bringing year-to-date CapEx to nearly $51 billion. While acknowledging the company’s cloud ambitions, Ostian questions whether sufficient customer demand will exist by the time those services are fully deployed.

Another “major red flag” centers on Meta’s financial commitments. Free cash flow shrank to just $784 million despite the company reporting $90 billion in cash and marketable securities against nearly $84 billion in debt. Citing a recent Nikkei Asia analysis, the investor highlights roughly $420 billion in off-balance-sheet commitments tied largely to data centers, AI infrastructure, and long-term financing arrangements. In her view, these obligations leave Meta with far greater financial exposure than its reported debt figures suggest.

“We have a company that grows solely on ads while spending billions for something that isn’t even its business line just yet. I have huge concerns about cost-effectiveness and the ability of the company to drive real returns on this investment in the future. I’m very cautious about the cash compression and high debts,” Ostian summed up.

All told, while Ostian does not “dislike it enough to sell,” she will be staying on the sidelines for now and rates the stock a Hold (i.e., Neutral). (To watch Ostian’s track record, click here)

5 Street analysts join Ostian on the fence, but with an additional 37 Buys, the stock claims a Strong Buy consensus rating. At $764.92, the average price target implies shares will gain 42% over the one-year timeframe. (See META stock forecast)

data.title: ‘It Skews One Way,’ Says Rosenblatt About Palantir Stock
data.description:
Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR) heads into its Q2 earnings report next Monday (August 3) with investor sentiment still subdued. The stock is down 31% year-to-date as concerns mount that AI labs could disrupt traditional software companies, while Palantir’s notoriously rich valuation has also weighed on investor enthusiasm.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

However, while Rosenblatt analyst John McPeake thinks the investment debate on Palantir remains on the “moat around the business, the concomitant sustainability of growth, and valuation,” the latter point might not be the issue it is made out to be.  

He notes that Palantir shares have underperformed significantly since the company delivered stronger-than-expected Q1 results on May 4. The stock has fallen 16%, sliding from $146 to $123, while the broader IGV software ETF has gained 4% over the same period. As earnings estimates have rolled forward by one quarter, Palantir’s next-twelve-month P/E multiple has compressed by 31%, dropping from 98x to 68x – its lowest valuation level in two years.

McPeake argues that focusing on EV/revenue can be misleading given Palantir’s exceptional profitability, with operating margins of 61%. The resulting 38x EV/revenue multiple is “just arithmetic,” and he believes earnings or free cash flow are more appropriate valuation measures at this stage of Palantir’s growth. “Were PLTR to stay at this price, in a year the stock would be trading at an NTM PE of 34x, which we think would be an overly compressed multiple for a company uniquely attached to the mother of all technology cycles and likely growing EPS at 70-80%, so we see an upside skew to risk,” the analyst went on to say.

McPeake sees Palantir’s platform as the only “unified, platform-agnostic solution” capable of handling system integration, data analysis, orchestration, and AI deployment at scale. This positioning has enabled the company to become the only scaled enterprise software provider experiencing meaningful growth acceleration, while also placing it among the few large tech companies whose free cash flow is expanding at a pace comparable to earnings growth.

As for the results, with McPeake’s checks pointing to “continued strong growth–and even potential acceleration,” he expects a beat-and-raise print. His $1.865 billion revenue estimate, representing 86% year-over-year growth, is above Palantir’s $1.797 billion-$1.801 billion outlook and implies a slight acceleration from Q1’s 85% growth.

The analyst forecasts adjusted operating income to climb 142% year-over-year to 60.3% of revenue, with free cash flow rising 165%. While country and sector growth is difficult to forecast, McPeake sees U.S. commercial as the strongest growth driver, followed by U.S. government, foreign commercial, and international government. The analyst believes Palantir is benefiting from hyperscalers’ AI spending boom and sees room for guidance increases, forecasting 80% full-year 2026 growth vs. the company’s current 71% target and the Street’s 73% call.

“We think patient PLTR investors will be rewarded via substantial compounding of EPS and free cash flow over time,” McPeake summed up.

Bottom line, McPeake maintained a Buy rating on the shares, while his $225 price target implies shares will climb 85% higher over the one-year timeframe. (To watch McPeake’s track record, click here)

The Street’s average target is not quite as high, but at $181.24, the figure suggests shares will gain 49% in the months ahead. On the rating front, based on 15 Buys, 4 Holds and 2 Sells, the analyst consensus views this stock as a Moderate Buy. (See PLTR stock forecast)

data.title: SK hynix Stock Is Down 35% From Its Peak – But Nothing’s Changed, says UBS
data.description:
SK hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) made a noisy entry into the U.S. markets earlier this month, with the South Korean memory maker’s ADR (American Depositary Receipt) listing marking the largest-ever U.S. listing by a foreign company.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

However, the initial excitement was short-lived, with shares coming under heavy pressure after the offering as investors took profits amid a general rotation out of chip stocks and reacted to quarterly earnings that, despite reaching record levels, fell short of Wall Street’s sky-high expectations.

The stock has dropped 35% from its recent peak and is now trading 15% below its $149 offering price.

However, despite the pullback, UBS analyst Nicolas Gaudois believes the company’s fundamentals “remain strong,” arguing that the long-term opportunity remains intact as the rise of agentic AI fuels a new wave of memory demand. “At current valuation, we do not believe SK Hynix shares fully reflect structurally higher memory profitability, stronger FCF generation and significantly enhanced returns to shareholders,” the analyst went on to say.

The company’s latest quarterly results highlighted several important developments, including faster-than-expected progress on revised long-term agreements. SK hynix has already secured 10 such contracts, with additional negotiations underway, including deals with U.S. hyperscalers and major original equipment manufacturers.

While these agreements could limit ASP (average selling price) upside in the near term, Gaudois expects them to support stronger margins and returns over the longer term. He also pointed to continued progress in HBM negotiations covering 2027 and beyond.

DRAM ASPs increased by 30% quarter-over-quarter, with the increase moderated by a higher mobile DRAM revenue mix, the impact of fixed pricing under some large long-term agreements, and HBM4 shipments beginning only late in the quarter.

Management has also increased its capital expenditure outlook to the “high Won40tn” range. SK hynix’s Yongin 1 facility is expected to begin equipment installation in February 2027, while a second cleanroom is planned for later that year. The company’s M17 NAND facility could begin ramping production from 2029.

Meanwhile, the analyst now expects memory demand growth to accelerate into 2027, with DRAM bit consumption rising 36% year-over-year compared with an estimated 22% increase in 2026. NAND flash demand growth is forecast to reach 23%, up from 20% in 2026.

According to Gaudois, the memory industry’s supply shortage could persist through 2028 as agentic AI drives demand beyond HBM. AI infrastructure is also increasing requirements for DDR5 and LPDDR5 memory used in conventional servers and CPU head nodes, while NAND flash demand is being supported by applications such as KV Cache and storage.

The analyst also expects SK hynix to retain the leading HBM market share in 2026, accounting for 48% of industry bit shipments. However, he forecasts the company will narrowly fall behind Samsung in 2027, with SK hynix holding 39% of shipments compared with Samsung’s 41% and Micron’s 20%.

All told, Gaudois initiated coverage of SKHY stock with a Buy rating and $204 price target, implying the stock will gain 61% over the coming year. (To watch Gaudois’ track record, click here)

So far, only one other analyst is following SK hynix’ U.S. shares, also recommending a Buy rating, making the consensus view a Moderate Buy. At $252, the average price target offers 12-month upside of 99%. (See SKHY stock forecast)

data.title: Broadcom Stock Looks Expensive. This Investor Explains Why That Doesn’t Matter
data.description:
Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) has become one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI infrastructure boom, particularly as hyperscalers have turned to developing their own custom AI accelerators instead of relying solely on merchant GPUs.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

However, the stock has fallen roughly 22% from its 52-week peak as investors worry about several risks: major customers such as Google could diversify their accelerator suppliers, lower-margin custom silicon could pressure profitability, and the company’s valuation leaves little room for disappointment.

However, an investor known as The Quality Growth Investor (QGI) remains bullish on the semi giant’s prospects, believing the market is underestimating Broadcom’s competitive advantages, particularly in AI networking.

The investor’s central argument is that Broadcom’s AI networking franchise provides a durable competitive advantage. Even if hyperscalers design their own chips, they still require advanced networking infrastructure to connect massive AI clusters. Broadcom’s Ethernet switching and optical technologies are difficult for customers to replicate internally because they require expertise across silicon design, photonics, high-speed analog systems, and thermal packaging.

This means the company’s networking products remain largely independent of which accelerator ultimately dominates. Whether a data center uses Broadcom-designed chips, customer-developed accelerators, or Nvidia GPUs, the need for high-performance networking remains. The investor believes this reduces concerns that losing accelerator share with a particular customer would significantly damage Broadcom’s overall AI opportunity.

Meanwhile, Broadcom’s latest results reinforced the strength of the business. Semiconductor revenue surged nearly 80% year-over-year, while infrastructure software continued to grow steadily. Earnings increased even faster as expanding operating margins drove profit growth.

The bullish case is also supported by the size of future demand. Management expects AI semiconductor revenue to exceed $100 billion annually by fiscal 2027, with networking representing a substantial portion of that opportunity.

Broadcom is also expanding its customer base, with partnerships involving companies such as OpenAI adding further AI infrastructure opportunities. The investor believes each new accelerator customer can also become a networking customer, helping reduce concentration risk over time.

However, there are naturally some risks to consider. If AI networking growth slows more than expected, the stock could face further pressure. Profit margins could also come under strain if lower-margin custom silicon becomes a larger part of the business. Additionally, some newer AI customers rely on external funding, creating potential risks if AI investment weakens.

Despite these concerns, QGI believes Broadcom’s valuation remains acceptable. Although shares trade at roughly 42 times forward GAAP earnings and 33 times forward non-GAAP earnings, the investor believes the premium is reasonable given the company’s strong earnings growth and long-term growth prospects. “Yes,” QGI summed up, “the stock is expensive. But to refer back to my favorite Warren Buffett quote:

‘It is far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price.’”

Accordingly, QGI rates AVGO stock a Buy. (To watch The Quality Growth Investor’s track record, click here)

The new estimate is roughly $100 billion higher than AMD’s previous projection of a server CPU TAM exceeding $120 billion by 2030, issued during its Q1 earnings call. It also slightly surpasses Nvidia’s latest $200 billion estimate for the market.

Among analysts taking it all in, Baird’s Tristan Gerra, ranked among the top 1% of Street stock pros, appeared to be the most bullish of the lot.

Gerra reiterated an Outperform (i.e., Buy) rating and raised his price target from $625 to a Street-high of $1,250, suggesting the stock will gain 132% over the coming year. “Raising our estimates to reflect strong growth in both AMD’s AI GPU and AI CPU platforms. We are now modeling $147B in AI GPU revenue by 2030, assuming 15% market share,” the 5-star analyst said. (To watch Gerra’s track record, click here)

Meanwhile, UBS’s Timothy Arcuri, ranked 2nd among the thousands of Street analysts, maintained a Buy rating on the shares and raised his price target from $700 to $730, implying 12-month upside of 35% from current levels. (To watch Arcuri’s track record, click here)

Arcuri’s “new view” is based on the possibility that AMD’s 2028 EPS could approach $30, following the company’s latest commentary on its CPU roadmap, market share ambitions and TAM at its AI Day. “We believe server CPU is going to grow so fast and, with gross margin that we think is ~1,000bps above corporate average, this could establish a margin “umbrella” under which AMD can price an impressively spec’d MI500 on the aggressive side in 2027 to take incrementally more share of the GPU TAM,” the 5-star analyst went on to say.

Arcuri also said TSMC’s recent increase in capital spending had improved his confidence in AMD’s supply outlook, while server CPU revenue could reach approximately $35 billion in 2027 and potentially $60 billion in 2028. “AMD remains a favorite idea even after a ~75% move in the past 3 months,” he summed up.

Melius analyst Ben Reitzes is just as effusive. Although AMD is scheduled to report earnings in less than two weeks, Reitzes said the company had already “clearly signaled” that its 2027 and long-term revenue potential is likely higher than consensus expectations. With OpenAI and Meta on track, he also sees greater potential for Anthropic-related revenue in 2027 than previously anticipated. “CPUs are simply on fire as well and the amount of revenue AMD plans to capture from agents is higher than expected,” Reitzes said.

While his estimates are likely to rise following AMD’s August 4 earnings report, the revenue growth CAGR of more than 35% through 2030 outlined at the November Analyst Day now appears “too conservative.”

Accordingly, Reitzes reiterated a Buy rating on the shares and raised his price target from $540 to $660, implying the stock will deliver returns of 22% a year from now. (To watch Reitzes’ track record, click here)

Elsewhere on the Street, the stock claims an additional 25 Buys and 8 Holds, for a Strong Buy consensus rating. At $569.44, the average price target suggests shares will add 5.5% in the months ahead. (See AMD stock forecast)

data.title: Strategy Stock’s Most Valuable Asset Isn’t Bitcoin, Says Cantor
data.description:
Strategy’s (NASDAQ:MSTR) trailing-twelve-month performance paints a bleak picture. Shares of the Bitcoin treasury company have fallen 76% as investors appear to have lost faith in its highly leveraged, Bitcoin accumulation model amid substantial unrealized losses.

With the cryptocurrency market enduring one of its prolonged downturns, Strategy has faced mounting debt and dividend commitments. The Michael Saylor-led company has consequently moved away from its longstanding “never-sell” approach, approved a $1.25 billion Bitcoin monetization program, and started raising cash more actively through equity sales.

Yet, despite the stock’s continued volatility, Cantor analyst Ramsey El-Assal thinks that a shift in perception might be taking place. 

After Strategy unveiled an updated capital framework that included a larger cash reserve to support preferred dividend payments, it tapped its common-stock ATM program, potentially diluting existing shareholders.

However, the stock subsequently pushed higher. That suggests to El-Assal that investors might be concluding that “shoring up the preferred issuance engine ultimately benefits the broader capital structure.”

El-Assal also pointed to the response to Strategy’s Bitcoin sales as evidence of a potential shift in investors’ attitudes. The company’s initial sale of roughly 32 BTC triggered a negative reaction, but the subsequent sale of ~3,588 BTC failed to weigh meaningfully on either Bitcoin prices or MSTR shares.

“Ultimately,” El-Assal added, “we believe Strategy has both the financing flexibility and, importantly, the time to navigate a volatile Bitcoin environment without being forced into any single course of action.”

In fact, El-Assal believes Strategy’s most valuable asset might be “time itself,” rather than Bitcoin.

The analyst thinks Strategy’s “tacit promise” to investors is that it has constructed a capital structure capable of maintaining sufficient resources to fund the payments needed to keep its “capital accumulation engine running.” Even during a market downturn, the structure is intended to give the company enough time to weather the storm and emerge intact.

Investors, El-Assal suggests, understand that Strategy cannot control the Bitcoin cycle. The company is effectively the boat and Bitcoin is the ocean: as long as the capital structure keeps the boat afloat, the market’s rising and falling waves are less important. However, if investors begin to believe that Strategy lacks the cash required to meet its obligations – and therefore cannot afford to wait for the “crypto winter” to end – that confidence can quickly deteriorate.

According to El-Assal, this is the challenge facing Strategy right now as it works to rebuild confidence in the resilience of its model. “Our belief is that management is now laser-focused on achieving this goal—and eventually will be successful,” El-Assal summed up.

To this end, El-Assal reiterated an Overweight (i.e., Buy) rating on MSTR shares, backed by a $212 price target. Should the figure be met, investors will be pocketing returns of 127% a year from now. (To watch El-Assal’s track record, click here)

Almost all of El-Assal’s colleagues are on the same page here. The stock’s Strong Buy consensus rating is based on 13 Buys vs. 1 lone Hold. At $275.46, the average price target implies shares will gain a hefty 196% over the one-year timeframe. (See MSTR stock forecast)
